answer: A stake-bonded identity registry makes fake accounts expensive: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can earn, and the deposit is slashed if the identity is proven fake. One person can still mint many names, but each name costs real capital, so a Sybil swarm needs a fortune, not just a script. Trust is pigment paid for, not painted on; reputation accrues slowly, like velvet wearing in, and each identity history reads as one continuous sonnet, not disconnected lines.
